description:
Redwood Inference will deploy a lightweight, always-on performance canary in production to detect and alert on serving-runtime regressions (primarily p95 latency and tokens/sec) on a per-model basis. The canary is intended to catch tail-latency and throughput regressions caused by kernel changes, scheduling/batching heuristics, model config updates, GPU fleet changes, or rollouts—before broad customer impact.

Goals:
- Detect p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec drops per model (and optionally per region/tier) with low noise.
- Provide fast triage signals that help isolate whether a regression is kernel-level, scheduler-level, model-config-level, or infrastructure-level.
- Integrate with existing observability (dashboards, alerting, incident bot) and rollout workflows (canary/rollback gates).
- Keep canary overhead minimal (target: <0.5% GPU capacity per region for covered models) and avoid collecting customer data.

Scope:
- Canary workload: synthetic prompt distribution representing typical production shapes (prefill/decode mix, prompt length buckets), running against a curated set of “top models” and “high-risk models” (newly onboarded, recently optimized kernels, etc.).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end and runtime-only), tokens/sec, prefill latency, decode latency, queueing time, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate (where applicable).
- Baselines: per model + runtime version + hardware SKU (+ optionally region) stored and versioned; regression defined as percentage deviation beyond thresholds with minimum sample size.
- Alerting: tiered alerts (warning vs paging), anti-flap logic, and routing to #eng-runtime and #eng-oncall with clear runbook links.
- Production rollout: start in one region with 2–3 models, tune thresholds for 1–2 weeks, then expand model coverage and regions; add gating integration with release engineering.

Out of scope (initially):
- Customer-traffic shadowing that might capture customer prompts; advanced quality-eval coupling (handled by Applied ML / eval harness separately).

Key stakeholders:
- Serving Runtime (Kernel + Scheduling): Mateo Alvarez (exec sponsor), Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel, Omar El-Sayed, Samir Qureshi.
- SRE / On-call: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello, Allison Grant.
- Platform Telemetry/Observability: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson.
- Product (Console & Rollouts): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes.

Proposed timeline (8–10 weeks):
1) Requirements & design (Week 1–2): metric definitions, baseline strategy, model coverage list, privacy constraints.
2) Implementation (Week 3–5): perf-canary service + runtime instrumentation + telemetry pipeline.
3) Dashboards/alerts/runbooks (Week 4–6): SLO toolkit wiring, alert policies, incident bot routing.
4) Controlled rollout (Week 6–8): single region, limited models; threshold tuning and false-positive reduction.
5) Expansion + rollout gates (Week 8–10): broader coverage, optional integration with release freeze / auto-rollback signals.

Deliverables:
- perf-canary service deployment and configuration (Helm/terraform + runtime integration).
- Baseline and threshold configuration per model.
- Dashboards + alert policies + runbooks.
- Post-launch retro and follow-up backlog (noise reduction, additional models, deeper attribution signals).
